contentHtml:
This easy one-pan cheesy beef penne skillet turns ground beef, pasta, tomatoes, and melted cheese into a filling family dinner without boiling the pasta in a separate pot. Everything cooks in one deep skillet, the sauce develops while the penne simmers, and dinner is ready in about 35 minutes.

It is the kind of dependable weeknight meal that works for beginner cooks, hungry families, and anyone who wants comfort food without a sink full of dishes. Add it to your weekly plan with Family Meal Planning Tools, then resize the ingredients for your household with the recipe scaler.

Easy One-Pan Cheesy Beef Penne Skillet Recipe

Prep time: 10 minutes
Cook time: 25 minutes
Total time: 35 minutes
Yield: 6 servings

Equipment

  • 12-inch deep skillet or Dutch oven with a lid
  • Wooden spoon or sturdy silicone spatula
  • Chef's knife and cutting board
  • Measuring cups and spoons
  • Instant-read thermometer

Ingredients

  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • 1 pound lean ground beef
  • 1 small yellow onion, diced
  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • 2 tablespoons tomato paste
  • 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning
  • 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce
  • 1 can diced tomatoes with juices, 14.5 ounces
  • 1 can tomato sauce, 8 ounces
  • 2 3/4 cups low-sodium beef broth, plus more if needed
  • 12 ounces dry penne pasta
  • 1 1/2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese
  • 1/4 cup finely grated Parmesan cheese
  • 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, optional

Numbered Instructions

  1. Brown the beef. Heat the olive oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and onion. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking the meat into small crumbles, until the onion is softened and the beef has no pink remaining. The beef should reach 160°F. Drain excess grease if needed.
  2. Add the flavor base. Reduce the heat to medium. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, Italian seasoning, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until the tomato paste darkens slightly and the garlic smells fragrant.
  3. Build the sauce. Stir in the Worcestershire sauce, diced tomatoes with their juices, tomato sauce, and beef broth. Scrape the browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
  4. Cook the pasta in the skillet. Stir in the dry penne and bring the mixture to a gentle boil. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 14 to 17 minutes. Stir well every 4 to 5 minutes so the pasta cooks evenly and does not stick.
  5. Check the texture. When the penne is tender with a slight bite and most of the liquid has become a thick sauce, remove the lid. If the pasta is still firm and the skillet looks dry, add 1/4 cup broth, cover, and cook for 2 to 3 more minutes.
  6. Add the cheese. Stir in 1 cup of the mozzarella and all of the Parmesan. Sprinkle the remaining 1/2 cup mozzarella evenly over the top.
  7. Melt and serve. Cover the skillet for 2 to 3 minutes, until the cheese is fully melted. Remove from the heat, let the pasta stand for 5 minutes, then finish with parsley and serve.

Doneness and Food-Safety Cues

  • Ground beef is safely cooked when it reaches 160°F in the center.
  • The penne should be tender but still hold its tube shape instead of breaking apart.
  • The finished sauce should cling to the pasta. It will thicken slightly during the 5-minute rest.
  • If the skillet begins to look dry before the pasta is tender, add broth in small amounts rather than pouring in a large amount at once.

Useful Cooking Tips

  • Use a deep skillet with a lid. The trapped steam cooks the pasta evenly, while the extra depth prevents the sauce from bubbling over.
  • Stir more than once. One-pan pasta can stick where it touches the bottom, so give it a thorough stir every few minutes.
  • Grate the Parmesan finely. It melts into the tomato sauce more smoothly than thick shreds.
  • Let the skillet rest before serving. Five minutes gives the pasta time to absorb the last bit of sauce and makes each serving easier to scoop.

Substitutions

  • Use ground turkey or ground chicken instead of beef and cook poultry to 165°F.
  • Use rotini, rigatoni, or small shells in place of penne. Cooking time may vary by a few minutes.
  • Replace mozzarella with Monterey Jack or a mild cheddar blend.
  • Add 1 diced bell pepper with the onion for an extra vegetable.
  • Stir in 2 packed cups of baby spinach immediately before adding the cheese.
  • Use gluten-free pasta and confirm that the broth and Worcestershire sauce are gluten-free when needed; begin checking the pasta early because gluten-free shapes soften at different rates.

Storage and Reheating

Cool leftovers promptly and refrigerate them in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Reheat individual servings in the microwave in 45-second intervals, stirring between intervals. Add a tablespoon of beef broth or water before reheating if the pasta looks dry.

For the stovetop, warm the pasta in a covered skillet over low heat with a small splash of broth. Freeze cooled portions for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating for the best texture.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I use already-cooked pasta?

Yes, but reduce the beef broth to about 1/2 cup. Make the beef and tomato sauce first, then fold in 4 to 5 cups of cooked penne and heat it through before adding the cheese.

Why is my pasta still firm?

The heat may be too low, the lid may not fit tightly, or your pasta shape may need more liquid. Add 1/4 cup broth, cover, and continue cooking for 2 to 3 minutes before checking again.

Can I make this less cheesy?

Use 1 cup mozzarella and skip the Parmesan. The tomato-beef sauce will still coat the pasta well.

Estimated Nutrition

Estimated per serving: about 530 calories, 32 grams protein, 52 grams carbohydrates, 21 grams fat, and 4 grams fiber. Nutrition varies with the beef, cheese, broth, pasta brand, and serving size.
